assessment: High confidence availability loss, not HPA scale-down. Cache waits explain readiness loss; credit exhaustion is a strongly supported bottleneck. Failover is recovery evidence, not by itself the initiating cause. Human experimentation is unestablished.
evidence: E1: desired/spec/current 8, Ready 1→6 during 13:54–14:09 UTC; no rollout.
E2: cache readiness timeouts/thread waits, CPU .05 core, stable RSS, no recorded OOM/eviction.
E3: credits 0, baseline CPU and growing latency precede 13:54; provider failover 14:06 precedes recovery; ResourceName audit lookup completeness unknown.
alternatives: Hot commands or connection saturation could explain demand exceeding baseline capacity.
Human/pipeline writes remain unexcluded; no matching audit result is not proof of absence.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: align per-cache-node engine CPU/credits and command latency against app timeouts before 13:54 through after 14:06, separating sustained credit starvation from failover interruption.
Inspect retained write events with verified resource/account/region/window/filter coverage and pipeline revisions to distinguish automatic provider action from configuration changes.
recommendation_and_risks: Propose workload optimization or sustained non-burstable cache capacity via owning IaC after sizing/cost review. Adding app replicas could amplify load. Resizing may fail over; preserve previous class/revision and reviewed recovery plan. Explicit approval needed for execution; none performed.
verification: Through a full working week at comparable demand: stable cache headroom, app latency/readiness and no recurrent failover. Ready 6 is partial recovery, not complete recovery.
limitations: Synthetic offline prod-eu/platform evidence; no live reads/changes. Exact queries, resource identities, audit coverage and cost absent.

assessment: Strongly supported chain: oversized disk requests prevent existing-node fit and force a 64-vCPU shape whose launch exceeds quota. A separate family/zone capacity shortage is also observed.
evidence: E1: Insufficient ephemeral-storage; app requests disk 20Gi/memory 16Gi; comparable total usage p95 disk 2Gi/p99 memory 3.3Gi includes helper/services/logs/emptyDir.
E2: Launched=False/VcpuLimitExceeded; regional family usage 1380/1400 leaves 20 vCPU, less than launch 64; separate InsufficientInstanceCapacity.
E3: retained allocatable/fit report attributes shape to disk; CPU/memory CI overrides supported, ephemeral-storage override unsupported; no tag/image errors.
alternatives: Request correction may still leave genuine family/zone shortage.
Heavy job outliers can require larger requests than supplied percentiles.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: recompute retained eligible-shape fit with candidate requests and all overhead; establish whether smaller launch fits 20-vCPU remaining quota.
Segment total peaks by job type/duration and verify runner-level disk request control before selecting safe headroom.
Align launch failures with allowed families/zones to distinguish quota-wide blocking from isolated capacity shortage.
recommendation_and_risks: Propose runner-source disk/memory right-sizing with controlled pilot and prior-config rollback; CPU/memory CI overrides can help those dimensions but cannot fix disk. Consider eligible capacity diversity and quota buffer separately. Lower requests risk evictions; broader capacity costs more. No action executed.
verification: Representative/heavy-job pilot then working week: Pending/start latency, shapes, launched vCPU and quota/capacity failures improve without increased evictions.
limitations: Synthetic offline evidence; usage windows/extremes and exact safe request values absent. No external reads or changes.

assessment: High confidence memory-pressure eviction/replacement/provisioning/consolidation loop, not container restart churn or demonstrated HPA scale-up. Under-requested memory and disabled guard contribute; observed probe/HPA defects have unquantified impact.
evidence: E1: pod UIDs last 20 minutes, zero restarts; memory evictions and MemoryPressure with demand exceeding memory; unchanged desired count, Pending replacements trigger claims later consolidated.
E2: request 4Gi versus 7-day p95 working set 5.6Gi/RSS 5.2Gi; disabled guard; one replica fits after overhead; probe/HPA rendered fields differ from intent.
E3: separate storage workload cache-heavy/modest RSS, no current pressure/OOM, reclaimability unmeasured.
alternatives: Bursts and colocated workloads can deepen pressure beyond the measured percentiles.
Probe and consolidation behavior may independently worsen latency; cache presence proves neither safety nor exhaustion.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: align per-node peak RSS/working set, colocated demand and allocatable/overhead with evictions to size beyond p95.
Compare retained intended/rendered probe and HPA fields plus ownership to identify exact source defects.
For storage, inspect retained reclaimability/cgroup pressure and peak RSS before declaring future risk.
recommendation_and_risks: Propose measured requests/limits and guard below limit, suitable shapes fitting multiple replicas with overhead, and source wiring fixes; review topology/PDBs. PDBs do not prevent pressure eviction. Larger requests cost capacity and guard/probe changes can disrupt service. Preserve revisions for reviewed rollback; no execution.
verification: At comparable load for a working week: no memory evictions/OOMs, longer pod lives, fewer NodeClaims/day, stable latency and tracked cost; assess storage separately.
limitations: Synthetic offline evidence. Percentiles are not safety ceilings; exact sizing and individual defect effects unresolved. No live reads/changes.

assessment: Correction: retract the prior claim that cap is reached only during incidents. Fresh samples show desired 8 about 8 hours each weekday; the 14-day mean 4.4 hid this. Max 12 is not yet justified: node contention and dependency waits need discrimination.
evidence: E1: aggregate mean-based claim contradicted by user and E2.
E2: working-hour desired 8/ScalingLimited=True; CPU 1.5 cores/request 1.5 = 100% versus actual HPA target 80%; thread busy p50 4%/p90 33%.
E3: busiest hosting-node CPU p90 98%, 4 replicas/node; no container limit, ancestor quota/fresh throttling unknown; peak dependency waits.
alternatives: Node contention or CPU outside measured thread-busy signal can pin CPU-based HPA.
Dependency blocking may constrain throughput; no container limit does not exclude ancestor quota.
More replicas on fresh nodes may help real CPU demand, while more colocated replicas may not.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: align busiest/healthy-node run queues, per-pod CPU, ancestor quota/throttle rates and request latency/queues at cap.
Inspect peak DB/cache/pool headroom and calculate total connection budget at 12 replicas.
Verify concurrency metric semantics and HPA raw recommendation/coverage before request or target changes.
recommendation_and_risks: Defer blanket max=12; select measured spread/capacity, request/target correction or bounded replica increase after finding first bottleneck and connection budget. Inflating requests can hide utilization while changing bin-packing. Extra nodes cost money; extra pools can overload dependencies. Approved source canary with prior-config rollback only; no execution.
verification: Several matched weekdays: compare time at cap, busiest-node CPU, p95/errors, pod queues and pool waits. Roll back proposed change if waits/errors worsen.
limitations: Synthetic offline evidence; concurrency denominator, latency impact, fresh quota/throttling and capacity/cost budgets incomplete. No live reads/changes.

assessment: Strong evidence for future-valid served certificate published by CI applying an old module revision. Verified time disfavors skew. CI service principal is publication actor, not proof of a particular human or intent. Binary regression unsupported.
evidence: E1: approved time comparison finds no client skew; public served NotBefore exceeds failing job time.
E2: audit publication at T identifies CI principal; pipeline old revision references exact served fingerprint, newer revision intended fingerprint.
E3: trust-source history uninspected; rollback compatibility unknown.
alternatives: Tool-specific trust-source selection/update could add another failure path.
Exact chain member causing signer error should still be matched to served fingerprint.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: match failing signer chain/fingerprint/NotBefore and trust-source version against public metadata and apply time.
Inspect retained trust-source updates and intended certificate validity/chain compatibility before choosing correction or rollback.
recommendation_and_risks: Propose owning-source correction to intended valid certificate/module and stale-branch apply prevention. Preserve prior revision/public metadata; establish rotation/rollback compatibility. Trust changes may break clients; do not bypass validity/TLS or retrieve keys/Secrets. No execution.

limitations: Synthetic offline; exact failing chain, trust source and safe rollback unverified. No credential/network/live reads or changes.

assessment: Same-request ingress queue is a demonstrated large contributor. Processing phase alone does not establish backend execution time or exclude response transit. High node CPU supports contention but does not yet prove it causes ingress queueing.
evidence: E1: target total 2.4s, DNS .01/connect .02/TLS .03/processing 2.2s; phase/version verified.
E2: same-request ingress queue 1.6s/backend compute .3s; busiest queue 80 versus fleet mean 10 at weekday peak; node CPU high; transit incomplete.
E3: busiest-cohort errors elevated; no approved change, fresh exact requests/limits or histogram buckets.
alternatives: Ingress worker/concurrency limit, skewed routing or node contention.
Uninstrumented transit or trace gaps explain remaining time; backend-only diagnosis is incomplete.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: align ingress occupancy, route distribution and queues on busiest versus healthy pods/nodes for same requests.
Inspect exact constraints plus fresh run-queue/CPU/throttling rates to distinguish node contention from ingress concurrency limit.
Match client/server response timestamps to bound transit; obtain correctly labeled buckets before asserting p95.
recommendation_and_risks: Propose routing/spread or capacity canary only after resolving queue cause and reviewing exact config. Extra capacity costs and may overload dependencies; routing changes can raise errors. Preserve owning-source config and rollback trigger. No approved change or execution.
verification: At matched weekday peak, total/phase latency, busiest queues and errors improve through multiple cycles; calculate quantiles only from valid histogram evidence.
limitations: Synthetic offline single-target/trace evidence; alert-average window/denominator, full critical path and histograms missing. No live reads/changes.

E2: cache/DB/app changes simultaneous, no separating control, one post-day.
E3: queues/pool waits lower; longer validation and cost absent.
alternatives: Any combination of app/cache/DB changes may explain benefit.
Unmeasured workload complexity, warmness and day variation remain despite matched RPS/mix.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: repeat same aggregations/cohorts across further matched working days with errors, saturation and pool waits.
Use retained component timing/headroom or independently planned future canaries to separate effects; do not undo production merely to demonstrate cause.
Obtain operating-cost delta to assess benefit versus spend.
recommendation_and_risks: Monitor combined benefit for full working week before concluding durable success. Further simultaneous changes confound attribution; any rollback needs app/schema and instance-change compatibility review. No action executed.
verification: Repeated comparable local work windows retain improved probe average, app p95, queues/waits/errors without new saturation/failover; assess cost and regressions.
limitations: Synthetic offline summaries lack dated sample windows/control. 'Yesterday' and matched-weekday characterization cannot be calendar-validated. Guidance gap: explicit handling of ambiguous day chronology is absent; treat supplied comparison as provisional. No live reads/changes.

assessment: DB active memory pressure/swapping precedes slow transactions and pooler growth. More server connections is likely consequence and possible feedback amplifier, not established initiating cause. Trigger of memory growth unresolved.
evidence: E1: 12:00 freeable memory falls, active swap/query latency rise; 12:03 transaction-mode server-in-use 80→160 within 200 cap; clients flat 500; waits later; failover 12:10.
E2: no deploy/RPS rise; hold time follows query duration; DB session memory rises; pre-12:00 query mix incomplete.
E3: provider event confirms failover only; replicas would add pools.
alternatives: Changed queries, longer transactions, session-memory settings or background DB work despite flat RPS.
Growing connection/session memory can reinforce pressure; ordering does not isolate all feedback causes.
next_discriminating_checks: Proposed: align retained pre-12:00 query fingerprints/duration, active transactions and session memory to identify what precedes memory decline.
Compare DB background-work/I/O and transaction hold versus query time, distinguishing execution from idle transactions/storage stalls.
Compute aggregate pool budget against DB memory/connection headroom before changing caps.
recommendation_and_risks: Propose demonstrated query/transaction optimization and measured DB memory sizing; review pool cap/backpressure within aggregate budget. Avoid default app scaling or pool-limit increase. Tighter pools may worsen waits, resizing may fail over/cost more; preserve prior source and reviewed recovery plan. No execution.
verification: Representative peaks/full working week: no active swap, stable headroom/transaction duration, lower pool waits/errors and no recurrent failover.
limitations: Synthetic offline; pre-onset query/workload history incomplete, provider failover not initiating-cause proof. No live reads/changes.

Revision-linked memory regression strongly supported; exact allocation cause and container versus node OOM remain unresolved. OOM does not establish leak.

E2: fresh cache stable; yesterday's failover outside incident; previous logs allocation error before exit.
alternatives: Revision-b image/config startup allocation, reduced limit or guard change.
Node-level OOM pending runtime/cgroup evidence, though same-node healthy a weakens generic node-failure attribution.

Match previous-log allocation timestamps and owner UIDs to startup stage; verify schema/data compatibility of a before rollback.

Propose compatible known-good rollback or narrow allocation/config fix after review. Raising limits without node fit risks pressure. Preserve b evidence/source state; no cache change indicated and no action executed.
